title: Remote access
subtitle: SSH, keys, scp, bastion, config, SFTP — flip for meaning and notes

cards.meaning: Telnet = unencrypted session; SSH = encrypted shell, forwarding, file transfer
cards.notes: Telnet = postcard; SSH = sealed envelope. Prefer SSH; Telnet is legacy only.

cards.meaning: X = one GUI app over the network; VNC = full remote desktop
cards.notes: X is network-transparent (client on remote, display local). VNC is server + client for the whole desktop.

cards.meaning: Create RSA key pair: id_rsa (private) and id_rsa.pub (public)
cards.notes: Default path ~/.ssh/id_rsa. Passphrase can be empty (convenient, weaker if laptop stolen).

cards.meaning: Private key never leaves your control; public key goes on servers
cards.notes: .pub travels into authorized_keys. OpenSSH refuses a group/world-readable private key.

cards.meaning: Remote account file listing public keys allowed to log in
cards.example: Append local id_rsa.pub contents to remote authorized_keys
cards.notes: Append if the file already exists — do not overwrite other keys. Match with -i private key.

cards.meaning: Log in using that private key file
cards.notes: -i = key file location. Cloud images often use *.pem instead of id_rsa.

cards.meaning: -l user, -p port, -v verbose, -N no remote command, -t force tty
cards.notes: -N useful for tunnels only. -t needed for sudo/menus; multiple -t if ssh has no local tty.

cards.meaning: Run a one-shot command remotely without an interactive shell
cards.notes: Quote 'cmd1; cmd2' so the local shell does not run parts locally. Feed a script with < script.sh.

cards.meaning: Force a pseudo-terminal so sudo (and menus) work remotely
cards.notes: Without -t, sudo often fails with “must be run from a terminal.”

cards.meaning: Forbidden by default; enable only via sshd_config + restart sshd
cards.notes: Prefer normal user + sudo. Editing sshd_config alone is not enough until sshd restarts.

cards.meaning: Copy files over SSH (same auth as ssh)
cards.notes: Colon after host starts the remote path. . = here. scp uses -P for port (capital P).

cards.meaning: Jump through a public bastion to reach a private host
cards.notes: %h:%p = target host:port. Two keys/users: one for jump box, one for private VM.

cards.meaning: Alias with HostName, User, Port, IdentityFile for short ssh names
cards.notes: ssh targaryen expands the stanza. chmod 600 the config. Can hold ProxyJump/ProxyCommand too.

cards.meaning: Interactive secure file transfer over SSH (not plain FTP)
cards.notes: Encrypted on port 22 unless sshd changed. WinSCP is a GUI for the same idea.

cards.meaning: SFTP-only jail: no shell; user cannot see above the chroot
cards.notes: Also disable tunnels/agent/X11 for that user. Apply with systemctl restart sshd.

cards.meaning: Apply /etc/ssh/sshd_config changes (root login, SFTP jail, ports)
cards.notes: A bad config can lock you out — keep a console session open while testing.
